name: io-uring-setup
why: io_uring_setup creates a ring a syscall-hooking sensor may not see; ring creation by a non-allowlisted process is the anchor
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for io_uring_bypass_behavioral.c's io_uring_setup record

name: io-uring-enter-only
why: io_uring_enter submits ring operations; the rule's second branch must fire on an enter even when the setup is out of the window
source: synthetic: a process issuing io_uring_enter (the OR's second block)

name: io-uring-register
why: io_uring_register configures an existing ring but is neither setup nor enter; it shares the io_uring surface, so flipping the syscall to either anchored name fires

name: classic-read-syscall
why: a classic read() is exactly the syscall io_uring replaces to evade a syscall-hooking sensor; it keeps the I/O surface but is neither ring syscall, so flipping the syscall name to either anchored call fires
source: synthetic: a process doing ordinary read() I/O instead of using a ring
